details.publicNotes:
Plisayashas swim freely across the sky, using thermal energy to hunt and defend themselves from assailants of all sorts. While plisayashas are sociable among their own family groups, they typically attempt to avoid strangers unless someone directly threatens or provokes them. Groups of plisayashas who have been forced to contend with hunters in the past are quicker to respond violently to incursions on their territory. While plisayasha meat isn't particularly appetizing, birds and fish cut out of their stomachs have become a delicacy due to the precise pattern of freezing and cooking the food is subjected to as it passes through their bodies. Though befriending plisayashas can be difficult, they have a soft spot for druids.

Plisayashas trace their origins to a colony of mundane penguins. Their distant progenitors—under the guardianship of a circle of druids—fled their ancestral home to escape an elemental cataclysm and embarked on a long voyage through the various elemental planes. As they passed through bitter blizzards and endured raging flames, the primal energies imbued in the penguins' bodies mutated, granting them an unusual constellation of powers associated with the conflux of multiple elements.

Always Going Home

Plisayashas don't have a land of their own, either on the elemental planes or elsewhere; areas of pure ice are too cold and areas of unbound flame are too hot. The habitats they prefer, zones of mixed fire and ice, are almost paradoxically rare. Plisayashas are a far-flung species, having flown and swam through countless environments on their quest for the perfect home.

Eligible Imbued Properties air, bane, burning barbs, constitution, dexterity, energy resistant (cold, fire, vitality), fire, fire shield, ice, sensory (low-light vision), throwing, wild, winged, wisdom

description.value: If a plisayasha takes fire damage after applying their resistance to fire, they lose their fire resistance and take @Damage[1d6[persistent,fire]] damage. After the persistent damage ends, they can regain their resistance to fire by spending 10 minutes submerged in cold water.

Trigger The plisayasha takes damage

Effect The plisayasha attempts to escape. They Fly or Swim, up to half their Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions based on movement.

Inhaling an immense amount of air, the plisayasha inflates their belly enormously and then rapidly expels a powerful gust of glacial air in a @Template[type:cone|distance:20]. Creatures within the cone take @Damage[4d8[cold]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:21] save. The plisayasha can't use Frigid Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Frigid Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is pushed 5 feet back from the plisayasha.

Critical Failure The creature takes full damage and is pushed 10 feet back from the plisayasha. If Frigid Breath's cold damage ended the persistent fire damage from Thermic Compound, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round.

The plisayasha spits a scorching, viscous glob from their mouth, dealing @Damage[1d6[persistent,fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:burst|distance:5] within 30 feet (@Check[reflex|dc:21] save negates). While a creature is taking this persistent fire damage, it also gains weakness 2 to cold. If the creature takes any cold damage while under the effects of Thermic Compound, the persistent fire damage from Thermic Compound immediately ends, after applying the cold weakness once. Unlike many other fire effects, Thermic Compound can be used underwater. The plisayasha can't use Thermic Compound again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Thermic Compound]]{1d4 rounds}.
